full_judgment:
This Rule arises out of an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the plaintiff petitioner against judgment and decree dated 26-5-1996 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Patuakhali in Title Appeal No. 172 of 1995 reversing those dated 26-9-1995 passed by Senior Assistant Judge, Patuakhali in Title Suit No. 198 of 1992 decreeing the suit. 

 4. The learned Assistant Judge after hearing the parties found that the defendant No. 2 was not justified in making new advertisement inviting application for the post of the Assistant Tahshilder and decreed the suit against which the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 98 of 1992. The lower appellate Court on consideration of facts and circumstances found that the petitioner's name was recommended but the authority did not accept the recommendation and being included in the provisional list of candidates for appointment no vested right accrued to the plaintiff and hence allowed the appeal dismissing the suit. 

 5. Against the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court the plaintiff as petitioner moved this court and obtained the present Rule. 

 6. Mr. AKM Zahirul Huq, learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff petitioner, submits that the lower appellate Court committed error in the decision not considering the fact that the plaintiff being successful in the written examination and subsequent interview was entitled to the appointment as Assistant Tahshilder and denying such right fresh advertisement by the defendant was illegal and the trial Court therefore correctly decreed the suit. He further submits that the lower appellate Court did not consider circulars dated 28- 1-89, 24-4-89, 26-8-89, 12-11-89, 26-2-90 and, as such, committed error in the decision in the impugned judgment and decree passed against the plaintiff. 

 9. In such view of the matter, there is no material produced by the plaintiff to indicate that the plaintiff succeeded to prove that any right accrued to him for being appointed for Assistant Tahshilder and moreover by cancellation of the results on the basis of illegalities and irregularities in the examination, government directed further examination. The plaintiff therefore had no locus standi to lay his claim for the decree sought for declaring him to be entitled to get the appointment in question. Moreover, simple selection of the name of the plaintiff in the list recommended by selection committee for appointment could not confer any right to appointment to the service of the government. 

 11. It therefore appears that the learned Assistant Judge without considering this vital aspect of the case passed the impugned judgment and decreed the suit disregarding the principles of law and the lower appellate Court in its turn on consideration of the law and fact and by elaborate discussion of the facts and circumstances and on reappraisal of the evidence on record correctly set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. And, as such, I do not find that the lower appellate Court committed any error of law occasioning failure of justice.
